source.snippet: 432 Linux kernel CVEs published in the last 24 hours (link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-cve-announce/)

problem_statement: Security and DevOps teams responsible for Linux infrastructure face an unmanageable CVE triage burden when hundreds of kernel CVEs are published in a single day, with no automated tooling to prioritize which vulnerabilities actually affect their specific kernel version and configuration.
target_segment: Security engineers, DevOps teams, and SREs at companies running Linux-based infrastructure at scale
notes: Buyer signal: security tooling is a well-funded category; teams already pay for Snyk, Wiz, Qualys, etc. The 432-CVEs-in-24h event (2026-07-20) is a concrete, recent stress-test of existing triage processes and creates immediate urgency. Opportunity: a kernel CVE relevance filter that cross-references published CVEs against a customer's running kernel version, enabled modules, and distro patch status — a layer above raw NVD/CVE feeds that existing tools don't handle well at this velocity.
